summary: This document updates RFC 6020 and amends IANA guidance on the uniqueness of YANG module and submodule names. It clarifies how modules and their revisions are handled by IANA.

plainLanguage.summary: Every book in a library needs a unique title so people can find the right one. This clarifies the naming rules for YANG modules and their versions.

questions: do yang module revisions keep the same name
subtitle: Only a YANG module's first version needs a unique name; later revisions keep that name and namespace.

tldr.problem: RFC 6020 says all YANG module and submodule names in the IANA registry must be unique, but the practice IANA actually follows, where revisions of a module share its name, did not match that guidance.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC replaces the uniqueness text so that only initial-version names and XML namespaces must be unique, while every revision must keep the name and namespace of the initial version.
tldr.outcome: The written rule now matches IANA practice, and this document becomes an additional reference for the YANG Module Names registry.

today: RFC 9890 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6020. The unit metadata shows no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: A Rule That Did Not Match Practice
sections.content:
RFC 6020 defines a registry for YANG module and submodule names, called "YANG Module Names". Section 14 of that RFC requires all module and submodule names in the registry to be unique. The RFC points out that the practice followed by IANA is not consistent with that guidance.

RFC 9890 amends the guidance so that it complies with how IANA registers modules and their revisions.
sections.plainLanguage: The rule said every name must be different, but in real life new versions of the same thing kept the same name. So the rule needed fixing to match.

sections.title: The Replacement Text
sections.content:
The old text said all module and submodule names in the registry MUST be unique and all XML namespaces MUST be unique. The new text says modules and their revisions are maintained in the registry, and then separates initial versions from revisions.

  • All initial version module and submodule names MUST be unique.
  • All XML namespaces of initial version modules MUST be unique.
  • All module and submodule revisions MUST have the same name as the initial version.
  • All module revisions MUST have the same XML namespace as the initial version.
sections.plainLanguage: The first copy of a book needs its own special title. New editions of the book keep that same title.

sections.title: IANA and Other Considerations
sections.content:
IANA has updated the "YANG Module Names" registry, under the "YANG Parameters" registry group, to list this document as an additional reference. The RFC says this is needed because its procedure is authoritative for assigning names in that registry.

The document aligns an IANA policy with existing practice, so it adds no new operations or manageability requirements and no new or increased security risks. The text of the document was previously part of a YANG guidelines draft.
sections.plainLanguage: The official list now points to this new rule as the authority. Nothing else changes for anyone.

cells: Old: XML namespaces MUST be unique
New: revisions MUST keep the name and namespace

references.text: Bjorklund, M., Ed., "YANG - A Data Modeling Language for the Network Configuration Protocol (NETCONF)", RFC 6020, October 2010.
